title: Australia Proposes New Rules to Give Users Control Over Social Media Feeds
subtitle: The government's 'my feed, my way' plan aims to let people turn off the computer programs that decide what they see online.

summary.en: The Australian government has introduced new reforms to give social media users more control over their digital experience. The proposed 'Digital Duty of Care' bill would allow users over 16 to opt out of algorithm-driven recommendations. These computer-generated feeds currently decide what content appears on a user's screen. Supporters believe this will reduce distractions and improve mental well-being. However, industry leaders warn that these changes could fundamentally alter how platforms function.
summary.zh: 澳洲政府推出了新的改革措施，旨在讓社群媒體使用者對其數位體驗擁有更多掌控權。擬議的「數位照護責任法案」將允許十六歲以上的用戶選擇退出演算法驅動的推薦機制。這些由電腦生成的動態牆目前決定了使用者螢幕上出現的內容。支持者認為，這將能減少分心並改善心理健康。然而，業界領袖警告，這些改變可能會從根本上改變平台的運作方式。

paragraphs.en: The Australian government has announced a major new plan to change how social media works for millions of people. Under the proposed 'Digital Duty of Care' bill, social media companies would be required to give users the choice to turn off the algorithms that control their feeds. An algorithm is a set of computer instructions that decides which posts, videos, and advertisements a user sees based on their past behavior. The government has named this initiative 'my feed, my way.'
paragraphs.zh: 澳洲政府宣布了一項重大新計畫，旨在改變數百萬人使用社群媒體的方式。根據擬議的「數位照護責任法案」，社群媒體公司將被要求讓使用者能選擇關閉控制其動態牆的演算法。演算法是一組電腦指令，會根據使用者的過往行為，決定使用者能看到哪些貼文、影片和廣告。政府將這項倡議命名為「我的動態，我做主」。

paragraphs.en: This proposal follows earlier efforts by the government to regulate digital platforms. According to reports from The Guardian, the goal is to allow users over the age of 16 to choose a chronological feed instead of one managed by artificial intelligence. A chronological feed shows posts in the order they were published, rather than in an order designed to keep a user watching for as long as possible. By making this change, officials hope to give people more power over their own digital lives and reduce the constant pressure of endless, machine-picked content.
paragraphs.zh: 這項提案延續了政府先前對數位平台進行監管的努力。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）的報導，其目標是讓十六歲以上的用戶能選擇按時間順序排列的動態牆，而非由人工智慧管理的動態牆。按時間順序排列的動態牆會依照貼文發布的順序顯示，而不是為了讓使用者盡可能長時間停留而設計的順序。官員希望透過這項改變，讓民眾對自己的數位生活擁有更多主導權，並減少不斷被機器挑選的內容所帶來的壓力。

paragraphs.en: To understand what this change might feel like, some users have experimented with turning off their algorithms manually. When a user limits their feed to only the accounts they follow, the experience changes significantly. Instead of being shown viral videos or advertisements, the feed becomes a simple list of updates from friends and family. However, as noted by The Guardian, this can lead to a feeling of being 'unmoored' or lost. Without the algorithm to suggest new content, a user might quickly run out of things to look at, revealing just how much modern social media relies on these systems to keep people engaged.
paragraphs.zh: 為了理解這種改變的感受，一些使用者嘗試手動關閉演算法。當使用者將動態牆限制為僅顯示他們追蹤的帳號時，體驗會發生顯著變化。動態牆不再顯示病毒式傳播的影片或廣告，而是變成一份單純來自親友的更新清單。然而，正如《衛報》所指出的，這可能會導致一種「失去依靠」或迷失的感覺。若沒有演算法來推薦新內容，使用者可能會很快就沒東西可看，這也揭示了現代社群媒體有多麼依賴這些系統來維持使用者的參與度。

paragraphs.en: Industry leaders have expressed concerns about these new rules. They argue that removing algorithmic recommendations could make platforms less useful and less interesting for the average person. Many social media companies rely on these systems to show users content they might actually enjoy, such as news, hobbies, or entertainment. If users choose to turn these systems off, companies worry that the overall quality of the user experience could drop. Furthermore, there are questions about how these platforms would continue to make money if they cannot show targeted advertisements based on a user's interests.
paragraphs.zh: 業界領袖對這些新規定表示擔憂。他們認為，移除演算法推薦可能會使平台對一般大眾而言變得較無用且較無趣。許多社群媒體公司依賴這些系統來向使用者展示他們可能真正感興趣的內容，例如新聞、嗜好或娛樂。如果使用者選擇關閉這些系統，公司擔心整體使用者體驗的品質可能會下降。此外，若平台無法根據使用者的興趣投放精準廣告，它們將如何持續獲利也引發了疑問。

paragraphs.en: Despite these concerns, the government remains focused on the potential benefits for mental health. Many people feel that social media has become a source of constant distraction, making it difficult to focus on real-life relationships. By giving users the option to step away from the influence of algorithms, the government hopes to create a healthier online environment. For some, the change is a welcome return to a simpler time, when social media was primarily a tool for connecting with people you already know.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些擔憂，政府仍聚焦於其對心理健康的潛在益處。許多人認為社群媒體已成為持續分心的來源，讓人難以專注於現實生活中的人際關係。透過賦予使用者選擇脫離演算法影響的權利，政府希望創造一個更健康的網路環境。對某些人來說，這項改變是回歸到一個更單純時代的樂事，當時社群媒體主要是一個與熟人聯繫的工具。

paragraphs.en: As the debate continues, the focus is shifting toward how these platforms will implement such a large change. If the bill passes, social media companies will have to redesign their interfaces to make the 'opt-out' feature easy to find and use. This is not just a technical challenge but a shift in the business model of the entire industry. While some users are excited about the prospect of a cleaner, more predictable feed, others are still adjusting to the idea of a social media experience that is not constantly trying to grab their attention.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著辯論持續進行，焦點正轉向這些平台將如何實施如此巨大的變革。如果法案通過，社群媒體公司將必須重新設計介面，使「退出」功能變得容易尋找與使用。這不僅是一項技術挑戰，更是整個產業商業模式的轉變。雖然有些使用者對擁有更乾淨、更可預測的動態牆感到興奮，但其他人仍在適應一種不再不斷試圖吸引他們注意力的社群媒體體驗。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the success of this legislation will depend on how many people actually choose to use the new controls. If only a small number of people opt out, the impact on the platforms might be limited. However, if a large portion of the population decides to turn off their algorithms, it could force a major change in how social media companies operate globally. The Australian government’s move is being watched closely by other countries, as it represents one of the most direct attempts yet to challenge the power of big technology companies over the information we consume every day. For now, the conversation remains centered on finding a balance between the convenience of modern technology and the need for more personal control.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，這項立法的成功將取決於有多少人真正選擇使用這些新控制功能。如果只有少數人選擇退出，對平台的影響可能有限。然而，如果很大一部分人口決定關閉演算法，這可能會迫使全球社群媒體公司的運作方式發生重大改變。澳洲政府的舉動正受到其他國家的密切關注，因為這代表了目前為止挑戰大型科技公司對我們日常消費資訊之掌控權的最直接嘗試之一。目前，對話的核心仍集中在如何於現代科技的便利性與對更多個人自主權的需求之間取得平衡。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Feeling lost, confused, or lacking a sense of purpose or connection.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 感到迷失、無所適從、失去方向感。
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意指船隻脫離繫泊處（漂流），這裡用來形容失去演算法引導後產生的心理狀態。文中：However, as noted by The Guardian, this can lead to a feeling of being 'unmoored' or lost.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To have nothing left of something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是常見的片語，但在這裡形容內容被看完，無法再滑下去。文中：Without the algorithm to suggest new content, a user might quickly run out of things to look at, revealing just how much modern social media relies on these systems to keep people engaged.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To choose not to participate in something or to stop using a service.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在科技與商業語境中常用，指主動選擇不使用某項功能。文中：If only a small number of people opt out, the impact on the platforms might be limited.

Under the proposed 'Digital Duty of Care' bill, users over 16 could opt out of algorithmic recommendations. This move follows previous efforts to ban children under 16 from major social media platforms. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese states the goal is to empower users rather than increase government control. Tech companies could face massive fines if they fail to comply with these new safety and transparency requirements.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary requirement for social media companies under the proposed 'Digital Duty of Care' bill?

options.A: They must remove all advertisements from user feeds.
options.B: They must allow users over 16 to disable algorithmic feeds.
options.C: They must redesign their platforms to be more profitable.
options.D: They must force all users to switch to a chronological feed.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，政府的目標是讓 16 歲以上的用戶能選擇使用「時間順序（chronological）」的動態牆，而非演算法推薦的內容。選項 A 錯誤，因為法案並未要求移除廣告；選項 C 錯誤，因為這是企業擔心的後果，而非法律要求；選項 D 錯誤，因為法案是提供「選擇權（choice）」，而非強制所有用戶切換。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might social media companies be financially worried about the 'my feed, my way' initiative?

options.A: They will have to pay a fine for every user who turns off their algorithm.
options.B: They will lose the ability to keep users on the app for long periods.
options.C: They will be unable to collect data on user preferences for targeted ads.
options.D: They will have to hire more staff to manage a chronological feed.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，企業擔心如果用戶關閉演算法，他們將無法根據用戶興趣投放「精準廣告（targeted advertisements）」，這直接影響了他們的獲利模式。選項 A 文章未提及罰款；選項 B 是演算法的功能，而非企業擔心的「財務」直接原因；選項 D 文章中並未提到需要增加人手，重點在於商業模式的改變。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the word 'unmoored' most likely mean?

options.A: Feeling disconnected or lacking a sense of direction.
options.B: Experiencing a sense of extreme excitement.
options.C: Being unable to access the internet properly.
options.D: Feeling overwhelmed by too much information.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到當用戶關閉演算法後，因為沒有系統推薦新內容，會感到「unmoored」或迷失。此字原意指船隻脫離了繫泊處，在文中引申為失去指引、感到無所適從。選項 B 與文意相反；選項 C 過於字面解釋，文中並未說網路斷線；選項 D 則與原文描述的「內容太少而感到空虛」的情況不符。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the proposed Australian legislation?

options.A: The legislation will certainly improve the mental health of all social media users.
options.B: Social media companies are planning to ignore the government's new regulations.
options.C: The government is trying to balance user control with the current digital business model.
options.D: The main goal of the bill is to stop people from using social media entirely.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章最後一段總結，這場辯論的核心在於如何在「現代科技的便利性」與「個人控制權」之間找到平衡。選項 A 過於絕對，文章僅提到政府的「希望」；選項 B 與事實不符，企業雖表達擔憂但未說要無視法律；選項 D 錯誤，法案旨在改變使用方式，而非禁止使用。
